summary: Polk County, TX steel tower carrying a house, described in a 1949 NGS survey record; listed as gone, with no removal date or site description found.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower supporting a house with a pyramidal roof
facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association index marks Moscow (Loc 1) as Tower Gone; no removal date or site description found

events.note: National Geodetic Survey station description dated 1949 describes the steel tower as standing, with a house at the top

evidence.supports: Station is about 7 miles southwest of Corrigan and about 5 miles west of the village of Moscow, on the highest point in the vicinity
evidence.quote: THE STATION IS LOCATED ABOUT 7 MILES (AIR-LINE) SOUTHWEST OF CORRIGAN, ABOUT 5 MILES (AIR-LINE) WEST OF THE VILLAGE OF MOSCOW, AND IS ON THE HIGHEST POINT IN THE VICINITY.

evidence.supports: Station is in Polk County, Texas
Station description was made by the Coast and Geodetic Survey in 1949

sources.title: Moscow
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (centraluslookouts.weebly.com), quoting the National Geodetic Survey

notes_for_editor: The NGS description gives no coordinates, so linking it to Loc 1 rests on the matching Moscow name and Polk County, plus the tnlandforms list placing a Moscow tower at the Loc 1 point. Check it against NGS PID BL2160 when the NGS site responds; that fetch timed out here. The 1949 date is the year of the NGS description, not a construction date, and the story says so. Height 110 ft converted to 33.5 m. The Forest Lookouts page is the only text for this datasheet and quotes it without a sourced date of construction. The tnlandforms TFS column is not explained in that list, so the agency fact rests on the Forest Lookouts page naming the Texas Forest Service. Moscow (Loc 2) at 30.90192, -94.91568 is a separate FFLA entry and is not researched. Budget: 0 web searches, about 4 page reads.
